subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the temple on the outskirts of Gurabad

732194801.text: "Make camp upon reaching your destination and seal the canyon to outsiders. Only members of the Tanit and the following tribes may pass..."

732194802.text: "...If you discover any who carry a Jinni bottle with them, take it. The bounty will be split as agreed..."

732194803.text: Huh, so they intentionally didn't go for Jeht, then?

732194805.text: Now, my master, we need not be hasty. Let us clear the next camp first.

732190701.text: You done, Azariq? You've bound your head up so tight that even Al-Ahmar himself would have trouble peeling your skin off! Who knows, he might even laugh at you for being a scaredy-cat!

732190702.text: Hah. Is that how you talk to your elders, little wildcat? Have you forgotten your actual business here? Or about how someone's been waiting for you for half a day?

732190703.text: Oh, and "someone" tanning themselves in the sun and having a drink or two passes for "business" now, does it?

732190704.text: Hmph. Woe to thieves who make false accusations! Just you watch: maybe I'll stick that clever little head of yours upside down in the sand. Maybe that'll clear it!

732190705.text: Rubbish, you haven't beaten me ever since you taught me how to wrestle.

732190706.text: You two get along so well.

732190707.text: Yeah, we've never seen two people start slinging mud at each other the moment they meet quite like you do...

732190708.text: Haha! Well, this is Azariq, a senior of mine in the tribe. He's like my older brother, and he's been a big help!

732190709.text: *sigh* Yes, yes, she treats me like a brother. And we'd get along better still, if she didn't like hanging out with the ladies more!

732190712.text: #{M#And so what? Do you have a problem with that?}{F#Hey, hey, quit it! Stop giving them the wrong idea!}

732190713.text: #Alright, whatever... {NICKNAME}, was it? Take care of her for me, eh? She's pretty good, but she likes charging into danger like a wildcat.

732190714.text: What was that? Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think you just said something bad about me!

732190718.text: #Hehe, don't you fret, {NICKNAME}'s a real experienced adventurer! Things will be fine here with Jeht. Just leave it to us!

732190720.text: Hahahaha! *cough* Alright, alright, let's talk business.

732190721.text: Matriarch Babel has asked me to guide you into these city ruins. I'll lead the way, so follow closely.

732190722.text: Oh, so that's what it was. That's the first we've heard of what we need to do all day!

732190723.text: Well, it wasn't all that convenient to explain our objective back at the settlement. The Matriarch believes the walls have ears.

732190724.text: Our objective here is to find the fragment of the Mother of the Jinn. We need it in order to be accepted into the Eternal Oasis at the desert's heart.

732190725.text: The Jinn were the familiars of the Queen of All Oases, so it will naturally accept their presence. Their powers were also intended to create fertile lands amidst barren sands.

732190726.text: So we... Well, Matriarch Babel, needs the aid of the Jinni to restore fertility to our tribe's soil, which will maintain the health of our herds.

732190727.text: Also, this particular Jinni still maintains her intelligence, so we should be able to pass through the seals on the Eternal Oasis with her aid.

732190729.text: Alright, that's that. To enter the ruins, we need to handle these mysterious devices first...

732190730.text: For example, this one seems to be able to blow sand away in a specific direction... Although I'd call it something more akin to "breaking a seal," really...

732190731.text: Whatever the case, even though the method to unlock them has been lost, some trial and error on my part has shown that heavy impact can change the direction it's facing, creating runes that flow.

732190732.text: That should rid us of those annoying piles of sand.

subQuests.subQuestName: Activate the device and open the gate
Activate the device and open the gate

732194101.text: Hey, why did you stop us? The thing we're looking for is just up ahead...

732194105.text: Look behind you — we're not alone.

732190901.text: The temple's safe. I don't see any enemies, monsters, or dangerous devices.

732190902.text: There's just this big thing... Heh. How interesting.

732190903.text: According to archaeological records left by people who came before us, as well as a stone slate that Aderfi got from within some ruins...

732190904.text: This big object over here is the main device that keeps the Mother of the Jinn sealed.

732190905.text: Just from basic observation, I'd say that it's connected to the machine next to it. Perhaps they can be made to move in tandem somehow.

732190906.text: Huh... So we'll need to unlock this one by the side here to move the big object in the middle...?

732190907.text: That's about right, I think. As for what happens afterward... I think we'll just have to cross that river when we get there.

732190908.text: Funny, I don't see any rivers.

732190910.text: So, I think we just need to repeat what we did at the gate... Let's crack this device open, shall we?

subQuests.subQuestName: Activate the device within the temple

732191101.text: Well, the machine has started, and the sand pile is gone... But the main device hasn't responded at all.

732191104.text: #Wait, {NICKNAME}. You're the only one here who can use the elements, right?

732191106.text: Well, what I mean to say is that unlike us, who need to borrow the power of ancient spirits, your elemental abilities are innate, yes?

732191109.text: Why don't you try touching this big thing over here?

732191110.text: Um... But... What if it turns out to be super dangerous?

732191114.text: You say that... But we should be careful all the same!

732192101.text: The records I've seen tell me that neither the mercenaries who came here nor those who used man-made Delusions were able to activate this device. But if you were to try...

732192103.text: Huh? Did I? Think you might need to clean your ears a little... the desert winds carry sand into them a lot, so I hear.

732192104.text: Don't worry, I've got your back!

732192105.text: Or so I say, but you should be careful all the same. Just tell me if you think that something's amiss!

subQuests.subQuestName: Touch the giant device at the temple's center

732196101.text: Is the conversation with Matriarch Babel over?

732196102.text: In that case... Let's take a short break.

732191302.text: Hah, that's what I thought... Looks like the device earlier smoothed out its charging... uh, circuits? Looks like it's showing us the location of three other devices, too.

732191303.text: I suppose that if we go to these devices, we'll be able to activate all four of these seal-breaking machines and clear the sand piles in front of us...

732191304.text: Aye, I think that's how it is... judging from my previous ruin-delving experiences, anyway.

732191305.text: Wow! You sure do know a lot... and here Paimon thought you were just some guy in a tribe somewhere...

732191306.text: Hey, hey, give the man some respect, Paimon.

732191308.text: Hahaha, what do you even mean by that, Paimon? I'm a tribeswoman myself!

732191309.text: Alright, alright. Enough chit-chat. Let's follow the directions we've been given and look for the other three devices.

732191310.text: Hmm... Let me think. Let's start here.

732191311.text: How do you know that we need to go this way first?

732191312.text: Haha. A desert dweller's intuition, perhaps?

732191313.text: Hmph... If we get lost, it's on your head!

732191314.text: Relax. Both of us are here. If things go bad, we can fight our way out... or flee to safety.

subQuests.subQuestName: Activate the device and, in turn, another machine somewhere within the temple

732191701.text: You can try changing the direction it's facing by hitting it. I think we can create runes that flow and thus clear the sand pile blocking our path.

732191702.text: Why am I not doing it, you ask? Haha, sorry, but we tribespeople have some taboos about this mysterious stuff... Can't be too careful and such...

732191902.text: Hmph... I did see this large device in some really old theses, but this is the first time I've ever seen a real one up close.

732194901.text: "...The outland traveler may be identified by: their golden hair and eyes, strange foreign clothing, and a small floating fairy by their side..."

732194902.text: "...If they have obtained a Jinni, take it from them, and if they have yet to, then dispose of them..."

732194907.text: My master, if I may, I would advise that you review your choice of friends. We had an old saying for this ilk...

732194908.text: "The only loyal desert-dweller is one whose shoulders have been pierced by iron loops."

732194909.text: We should be rid of all of them now. Let us return.

732195001.text: A lot of the ruined areas we've encountered on the way show signs of man-made damage... There might have been unrest here, or even a war.

732195002.text: I'm no researcher, so I can't really read any pattern in these markings, but I doubt that the fate of this temple was a peaceful one.

732195003.text: The books say that Gurabad was destroyed with searing fire and the great anger of the Jinn...

732195004.text: The Jinn? Perhaps... But it looks more like the work of a mob, soldiers, or perhaps even tribespeople like us... But who knows, eh?

732195005.text: But we can think about that later. I think this big guy here is our more pressing concern, no?

732195006.text: Indeed... Perhaps the other chambers are all structured like this one. Let's look around again, shall we?

732195008.text: Huh? Mark? Paimon didn't see you do that.

732195009.text: We use scented oils made from Wenut larvae, planting it to mark the path we must tread, so that if we do get lost, we can just follow our nose to find the way back.

732195010.text: Now I'll have you know that our wildcat's nose is very sharp. We hunters wouldn't get very far without her!

732195011.text: Stop saying all that stuff, Azariq!

732195013.text: And you! Don't you start with that nonsense too!

732195017.text: Well, it's the... larva of a Wenut. *sigh* Agh, I've seen them so often that I'm actually not sure how to explain what they are. Tell you what, I'll explain more on the way back...

subQuests.subQuestName: Scatter the dust around the sealing machine
Activate the device and, in turn, another machine somewhere within the temple

732192201.text: Alright then. Go touch the device in the middle of the temple. Jeht and I will make sure you're safe.

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for a way back to the temple
Scatter the dust around the sealing machine
Activate the device and, in turn, another machine somewhere within the temple
Look for a way back to the temple
Scatter the dust around the sealing machine
Touch the giant device at the temple's center

732194505.text: Phew. That gave Paimon quite a fright...

732194506.text: ...That tremor's source should be to the north, outside the temple.

732194510.text: Right, that's true... Well, it's not like flying doesn't come with its own troubles, y'know?

732194513.text: #Let's go have a look, {NICKNAME}. Something huge is bound to have happened!

732194512.text: That's true... But wait. You don't either!

subQuests.subQuestName: Check on the situation outside the temple

732193305.text: A plaza with sides of seemingly equal length... and a new door's opened up on the opposite cliff. Is that our destination?

732193306.text: That's for you to explore, I fear.

732193307.text: Eh? Aren't you coming with us?

732193308.text: Sorry, but Matriarch Babel only asked me to open the way for you. You'll have to embark on the rest of the road yourself.

732193309.text: I trust that you can protect your friends, right, Jeht?

732193310.text: Oh, stop with that, you. What are you, my dad?

732193311.text: I know... Stay safe while you're heading back, you hear me?

732193312.text: #Of course. {NICKNAME}, you take care of Jeht as well!

732193313.text: Huh. Why's Azariq just up and leaving on us like that? Isn't he gonna go deeper into the ruins with us?

732193314.text: He's gone as deep as he wants to go, I think. These ruins are a cursed, taboo place to us Tanit... and the tribe's quite sensitive about that sort of thing.

732193315.text: But since I count as "half-outsider," I've got no qualms about going further. And anyway, you can't expect me to let you guys down!

732193316.text: And you did ask us to help you find this Oasis thingamajiggie anyway, right? We're with you to the end!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the ruins opposite the square

732194201.text: Ah, Jeht! And our guests! So you are here, after all.

732194202.text: "After all"? You trying to get familiar with us? We're pretty busy over here, so you'd better have had a good reason to stop us.

732194203.text: Ah, um... No, well, this... I was sent by Matriarch Babel with a message for you, Jeht. She has something urgent to discuss and would like you to, um... well, return to the campsite first...

732194204.text: This... That... What's got your tongue? Do you need me to shorten it for you? Did she say anything else?

732194205.text: She'd like to speak with you alone... Sorry. I didn't know you were in a bad mood...

732194206.text: A bad mood? Nonsense, I've never been better! You know, what with having found the Mother of the Jinn and all — which I'll be telling the Matriarch, of course.

732194207.text: #I'm more than pleased, and so will she be, I bet! And so will her "master," to have a nice new servant — wouldn't you say, {NICKNAME}?

732194210.text: #Matriarch Babel has business with me, so I'll take my leave now. My deepest apologies for not serving you to the end, {M#Prince}{F#Princess} {NICKNAME}.

732194211.text: Alright, let's go see the Matriarch.

732194212.text: S... Sure. As for you, honored guests, just follow this canyon, and you'll reach our camp soon enough.

732194215.text: Not much. I just thought that this child is quite interesting, that's all.

732194216.text: Really, though, she's got quite the temper...

732194217.text: She isn't... y'know, jealous of a bottle, is she?

732194218.text: You mean to say that she takes "a bottle" for her yardstick? Hah, perhaps.

732194219.text: Regardless, she is a good child. Trustworthy... if a little foolish.

732194221.text: Ah, see, I like you more already, my master.

732194222.text: Coming from you, that's kinda scary...

732194224.text: Oh, do not mistake my meaning, my master. I very much love the earnest impulsiveness of young women...

732194225.text: But she will be taught, my dear master... Trust me, she will.

732194226.text: Even if that happens, we'll pull her right outta the fire! That's what friends are for, after all!

732193901.text: Wow... The plants here have all withered... This doesn't look good.

732193902.text: No doubt, no doubt... And who shall we blame for that?

732193904.text: You obstreperous oaf... Where did you get that active yet actively useless tongue of yours, I wonder?

732193906.text: Are you... the Mother of the Jinn?

732193907.text: "Jinn"? Why, yes, I do count as one. "Mother"? Hmm... Well, if it does not displease you, I have been such before.

732193908.text: But "Mother of the Jinn"? Do those desert philistines wish to cajole me to laughter? I fear that this joke fails to amuse. It falls far short, in fact.

732193909.text: We have come on behalf of the Tanit tribe to see you, to ask that you show forth your great might and aid us in finding the place where Nabu Malikata slumbers...

732193910.text: Ah, so it is one of the desert folk. I like you, girl... You know the rules, and your manner of speech tickles me. Yes, you do amuse me.

732193911.text: Ah, but... Step aside for a moment. I shall have words with your lord only.

732193913.text: Mmm... The scent of unknown spices from afar... A servant girl of the desert-kin, and a flying pet...

732193914.text: #You must be a {M#Prince}{F#Princess} in exile, are you not?

732193918.text: Lilou... par... Wait a moment! You're... You're the one from the books...!

732193919.text: Speak not out of turn before your liege, sand-licking lackey!

732193922.text: That's right! Jeht isn't a lackey! You're too much!

732193923.text: Ah. Is that so? Oh, the tedium...

732193924.text: Ah... If my soul were not sundered into many parts, unable to muster sufficient strength... I could shift into any number of shapes that might please you.

732193925.text: A dancing girl, a lovely youth, an arhat or a yaksha... Or a lovely beast of those races that died out under the moon's light... I have been them all, and played all their parts, all for my lord's pleasure...

732193927.text: A lord I was willing to entrust my true name to... Yes, I did once have such a master. And today, I seem to have encountered his shadow.

732193928.text: You mean... Wait, wait a moment!

subQuests.subQuestName: Leave through the gap caused by the collapse

732194401.text: Hmm... Now, where should I begin...?

732194402.text: As the moonlight paints the stones white, and night wind blows chill, causing the tendrils of the campfire to snap and crackle... Amidst the calls of nocturnal birds winding across the distant sand dunes, the Jinni begins her tale...

732194403.text: Thousands of years have passed since the events told of in this tale. The desert had yet to become so desolate, and the oases spread out across the land like glittering jewels...\nIn those days, the Jinn walked the earth in great numbers, and they lived within the silver night wind and the flowing sands, in the ripples of the unknowable ocean, and in the pattering of the rainforest springs...

732194404.text:
We Jinn were not ordinary creatures, but we were the servants of the mistress of flowers.
We were untroubled by basic want, nor were we shackled by material thirst. It was "life" itself that greatly fascinated us...
The blooming and wilting of flowers, the gathering and scattering of birds — these were the things that held us in thrall.
Apart from that, only our "true names" could bind us.

732194405.text: We were carefree so long as our mistress walked the earth, and we enjoyed her eternal paradise, her love, and her comfort...\nBut tragedy would come, and our paradise crumbled as the mistress departed... Our revelry turned to mourning, and all that was good and lovely was violently perverted in that anguish...

732194406.text: And so we gave Al-Ahmar our true names, and became his servants... For he promised to find us our eternal companion, our true master.\nDeluded hope and trust did we harbor in our hearts, and so forsook our freedom, accepting imprisonment within silver bottles and servitude to his realm...\nBut what was lost was forever lost, never again to return.

732194407.text:
But do not think that the Jinn were wanton servants.
Only a love bordering upon madness could make the Jinn give their "true names" willingly.
For it was their deep love for the mistress of flowers that drove them to embrace the desert from the first.
Yet, waking to face the tomfoolery of this barren world caused a surly Jinni to fall incurably in love with the shepherd...

732194410.text: Not you, no... Hah, but much like you, my master. You were... much like him — as he was once.

732194412.text: Well now, girl, does that make you jealous?

732194413.text: #{M#No. It's just that I find this story quite familiar...}{F#Definitely not!}

732194414.text: #{M#That's because this story has happened before, and may yet happen again.}{F#Hah. She is quite transparent, my master. I once did have a daughter — my eyes are not deceived.}

732194416.text: *sigh* To the Jinn, "love" was a terrible chain, driving those who fell into its pit to make sacrifices, like the hyphae of a parasitic insect...

732194417.text: Oh boy, Liloupar's at it again with the scary analogies...

732194418.text: Hehe, we Jinn do not have this tedious thing you humans call "shame," so we do not shy away from discussing love, or revealing one's all to a lover.

732194419.text: #{M#*cough*!}{F#I'm suddenly glad that you're just a bottle now...}

732194420.text: But to the Jinn, this mad love could not be reconciled to betrayal. Or else, hatred and vengeance three times greater would be sure to follow.

732194421.text: That was the root of the farce that ended Gurabad... Though that is a different tale.

732194422.text: Actually, now that you mention it, I'd like to ask a question... Did you really have no other goal in presenting your "true name"?

732194423.text: Hmm? Hah, well, I suppose vigilance is wisdom.

732194424.text: Well, I do have something I seek. I wish to go to the Eternal Oasis, just as you do... There are things there that have been left unfinished.

732194426.text: Forgive me, dear master, if I can only slowly tell you that tale as our journey proceeds. But the time for that has not yet come.

732194427.text: But know this — it is good fortune that I should have met you.

732194428.text: Well, since we've got the same goal, let's get along. How about a toast?

732194429.text: And what shall you make this toast with? Me?

732194431.text: Alright, weird-story-time's over! Let's talk about something more relaxing.

732194432.text: #By the way, {NICKNAME}, do you play cards?

732194439.text: Eh, alright then... I for one shall not complain if a more elegant pastime were chosen.

732194440.text: Oh, that so? Shame, then. Why don't we talk about some of the things we've seen, then?

732194441.text: You all speak about the interesting things you've heard about, as well as the hair-raising adventures you've been through. Some absolutely ridiculous hearsay is even mixed in...\nThe three of you raise toasts to old triumphs, laugh at ridiculous tales, and shed tears and lament the sad stories.\nAt the end, Azariq closes the proceedings with a joke, and he absolutely kills it.

732194442.text:
#When the moon hangs highest, Azariq tells a rather coarse joke about a crocodile and a Sumpter Beast, which loses him his blanket-sharing privileges.
{M#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
She seems to have lived well amongst the Tanit since your last parting.}{F#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
A light scent of spices wafts from her, and it seems to you that all the stories she has to tell since your last parting seem tinged with this sadness.}

732194443.text: The night flies by as you chat.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.

732195101.text: #We're here! C'mon, let's find a place to sit and grab a bite, {NICKNAME}.

732195105.text: Haha, hardly that long! Good to see that you're all well. Jeht's really fond of you — we were just talking about you, in fact.

732195106.text: Eh? What did you talk about?

732195110.text: Oh! She did mention a little disagreement you had, yes... But you know, she talks quite carelessly, but isn't actually good at expressing her feelings.

732195111.text: Still, you should reflect as well. Jeht's very concerned about your safety, so you should pay a bit more attention to her suggestions.

732195114.text: Sorry, it was my fault, really. I was... petty. Childish.

732195115.text: I knew how important Liloupar was to our mission, but I threw a tantrum anyway...

732195116.text: Liloupar says stuff weirdly, and she does use some pretty creepy analogies...

732195117.text: But she looked out for us the whole way, so... Well, she's different from the people we've met so far for sure, but she doesn't seem like a bad person!

732195118.text: #Whatever the case... It'll be fine. {NICKNAME}'s important to you, isn't {F#she}{M#he}, Jeht?

732195119.text: #{M#Of course. You're my best friends.}{F#Yeah, I mean, I've always seen you as my... best friend, but I'm just worried that... *sigh* Never mind.}

732195121.text: Yeesh, you're so serious all of a sudden. Paimon doesn't know what to say at all...

732195122.text: Ugh, there's no need to be so awkward! I won't get mad anyhow from now on, and you can count on that!

732195123.text: Hahahaha! That's right, that's the spirit!

732195124.text: Ah, right! About the "Mother of the Jinn"... Is it with you?

732195126.text: Azariq! Didn't Matriarch Babel tell you not to ask that willy-nilly?

732195127.text: It's fine, Jeht! I mean, I guided you half the way, so I count as a "companion," don't I?

732195128.text: A "companion," you say? Perhaps you speak too hastily.

732195130.text: Such insolence! If you recognize me not, then your silence shall serve better!

732195131.text: Whoa, this is a pretty fierce one for sure... Is that the Mother of the Jinn, then?

732195132.text: I'd watch my tongue if I were you, desert-spawn.

732195133.text: This is Azariq, one of my brothers here in the tribe.

732195134.text: Hmph... Well, we could have chosen worse. This one is sturdy enough. A shame that he has too big a mouth, and too small a brain.

732195135.text: *sigh* How is talking to her supposed to *not* end as an exercise in frustration?

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the fellow who is up to no good

732194601.text: Wait but a moment, my master. Something is amiss up ahead...

732194602.text: Um... Do we really wanna pass this way, then?

732194603.text: ...It matters not. This is the path we must take, in any case.

732194606.text: I am sure, my master, that you too are able to sense the wicked intent ahead... But if we might discover who it is that ambushes us, we might yet turn the tables on them.

732194607.text: Things may indeed be perilous ahead, but you, O master mine, are the one to whom I have entrusted my fate. I shall go forth with you, and we shall face any obstacle together.

732194608.text: #Just relax! {NICKNAME}'s super strong, and no matter what, {M#he'll}{F#she'll} still have Paimon, right?

732194609.text: Hark, what did I say? Prepare yourself, master.

732194610.text: Hey, you guys... Aren't you Jeht's buddies?

732194611.text: Hey, c'mon, don't scare Paimon here... Why aren't they replying?

732194612.text: Well, if this is what it comes to... Do not forget to leave one alive, master.

732194613.text: We may follow that one's flight to find his allies and servants, and thus destroy their nest in one fell swoop.

732195302.text: You m—may d—do anything you please here in our camp...

732195304.text: Planting crops and f—feeding the fish. Sometimes, I also do some b—b—butchery. Crocodile skin and meat is v—very useful.

732195308.text: We get clean spring water all year around h—here, so it's just right for raising crocodiles. Th—that's why we fenced this place up.

732195309.text: Crocodiles are easy to care for, and they can be harvested for lots of skins and meat. Unfortunately, f—fields are a d—different story...

732195311.text: We do... but only for testing. Matriarch Babel invited some outsiders to c—c—come and provide us with Anahitian Blessing, and she got all these old books from the city...

732195312.text: S—s—so we've tried our hand at farming according to the contents of these books.

732195313.text: But the oases in the canyon are too narrow and lack nutrients. We need to find a way to f—fertilize the soil.

732195314.text: Tell me about the Anahitian Blessing...

732195315.text: The outsiders didn't want to reveal the fertilizer's composition. As such, we've had to rely on the people who provide it to f—fertilize the soil... which isn't good.

732195316.text: Th—that's why the Matriarch wants me to d—do some research here to r—reverse engineer our own Anahitian Blessing.

732195317.text: I shan't disturb you any longer.

732195318.text: Th—that's alright. Please take some crocodile jerky, dear guest. It's just over there...

732195306.text: Hehe, yes. I—I take care of them. These are quite large and obedient...

732195307.text: This one's c—c—called Sedim. Very fierce and strong, and skin's very vibrant. It'll make for a good satchel. And there's that one, Karam. It's small but plump. Rather gentle, too.

subQuests.subQuestName: Track your foe by following the footprints

732194701.text: "May this be testimony that we have provided the material support required for this ambush and robbery. As a token of friendship, the gifts shall be sent via specially-arranged Sumpter Beast caravan..."

732194702.text: "The Tanit tribe sends respectful greetings to the Afiyah tribe. May peace follow you, and may spices fill your storehouses."

732194703.text: Wait just a second! The Tanit tribe...

732194705.text: And that means... Ugh, were these guys hired by them?

732194706.text: Oho, so the desert people have learned to use books to keep records? Well, I suppose my awakening has given rise to fresh sights after all.

732194707.text: But what were they intending to do here, anyway?

732194708.text: Who knows? Most importantly, they were our foes.

732194709.text: Well, since we have found one part of a paper trail, we may as well search their encampment. There, I believe, we shall find more clues.

732194710.text: How do you know that's definitely the case?

732194711.text: Toads do not lay one egg at a time, and centipedes and scorpions huddle together in the damp shade.

732194712.text: Ugh, you and your creepy analogies again...

732194713.text: Whatever the case may be, we no longer need any of them in one piece. Let us proceed to the next encampment.

732195601.text: Hehe, so it's you... Youngster, I have heard that you and Jeht went into the accursed city. Ah, and you would like to know how I know this, yes?

732195602.text: Hunters have falcons and hounds to be their eyes and ears, naturally. But young one, I must remind you that this word, the "curse," comes not out of thin air.

732195603.text: A venom, the root of all tragedy, that drives all humans add, is hidden within a facade of flowing gold.

732195604.text: Perhaps it shall be so this time as well, that greedy prey shall fall into a trap, where they cannot be saved...

732195801.text: The night flies by amidst the card games and chats.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.

732196001.text: #Hah! Let's see what you'll have to say for yourself after {NICKNAME} thrashes you.

subQuests.subQuestName: Return to the tribal settlement and report to Babel

732194002.text: Allow me to dust you off. Jeht and Azariq are waiting for you as well.

732194003.text: We brought the object that you needed.

732194004.text: Jeht told me. Thank you both so much.

732194005.text: We were ambushed within the canyon on the way back.

732194007.text: We were attacked by your people while on our way back! There were lots of people hiding in the canyon, waiting to intercept us!

732194008.text: They were pretty scary, too! Do you know what all that was about?

732194010.text: No, I haven't a clue how that happened.

732194011.text: Traitors and exiles turning to banditry on the roads is quite normal, but the canyons here should have a lot of tributaries... It seems that I've underestimated them.

732194012.text: This has to do with Aderfi.

732194015.text: You give Aderfi's letter to Babel...

732194016.text: Aderfi... This is indeed his handwriting, and it is even signed in his hand. That he is a traitor is beyond doubt.

732194017.text: But... What if he's been set up?

732194018.text: Then he has still stained our honor with his name, and will accept his punishment.

732194019.text: However... *sigh* He left the camp some time ago, saying that he needed to go get some supplies from outside. I must apologize. I let my guard down.

732194020.text: You can be sure that we will exile that traitor, however. He shall not be permitted back into the Tanit hunting grounds — save in chains.

732194021.text: Please rest assured, you two, that I will get to the bottom of this on behalf of our tribe. I will not allow such happenings to go unanswered.

732194022.text: As for the "Mother of the Jinn"... Can I see her?

732194025.text: Honored Lady Liloupar, beloved servant of Nabu Malikata, founder of Gurabad, eternal prisoner of Ay-Khanoum, Babel of the mortal Tanit tribe seeks an audience with you.

732194026.text: *yawn* Mmm... Hmm? What did you say? Were you calling for me? I don't quite remember all those names.

732194027.text: Yes. We ask only, Lady Liloupar, that you lead us to the Eternal Oasis, to set us on the path to meet with the slumbering queen.

732194028.text: *yawn* So sleepy... My master, did you wake me to speak with this servant? *sigh* Why do you love consorting with these coarse folk so...

732194029.text: Well, then, Babel. Will you not dance? Amuse us, and we may yet grant you three wishes.

732194031.text: Hmm? What? Oh, I'm so sorry, you're the mother of this tribe, riiight! Hahahaha!

732194032.text: My apologies. I read the servility in your brows, and merely could not help but wish to see you dance and entertain us.

732194033.text: I am merely your servant and will listen to all you have to say. I shall follow the dictates of the Queen of All Oases, Nabu Malikata's will with due trepidation, and them I will not defy.

732194034.text: Hah! I shall not be so crude. Save your solicitations. I already have a master, and I do not intend to take on any servants either, so I fear your calculations have come to naught.

732194036.text: (...So Matriarch Babel can grovel too, huh...)

732194037.text: You have yet to see many things indeed!

732194038.text: My master, you hold my true name, I shall do what you, and only you, desire.

732194039.text: The decision shall be yours. I will not speak another word to these foul desert dwellers.

732194041.text: #Why, yes indeed, and it is this noble {M#prince}{F#princess} you see before you. Now, now, you need not kneel.

732194043.text: (C'mon, say something, why don't you!? Just look at her face!)

732194044.text: #I understand. In that case... Will you help us, {NICKNAME}?

732194301.text: #We're here! C'mon, let's find a place to sit and grab a bite, {NICKNAME}.

732194305.text: Haha, hardly that long! Good to see that you're all well. Jeht's really fond of you — we were just talking about you, in fact.

732194306.text: Eh? What did you talk about?

732194310.text: Oh! She did mention a little disagreement you had, yes... But you know, she talks quite carelessly, but isn't actually good at expressing her feelings.

732194311.text: Still, you should reflect as well. Jeht's very concerned about your safety, so you should pay a bit more attention to her suggestions.

732194314.text: Sorry, it was my fault, really. I was... petty. Childish.

732194315.text: I knew how important Liloupar was to our mission, but I threw a tantrum anyway...

732194316.text: Liloupar says stuff weirdly, and she does use some pretty creepy analogies...

732194317.text: But she looked out for us the whole way, so... Well, she's different from the people we've met so far for sure, but she doesn't seem like a bad person!

732194318.text: #Whatever the case... It'll be fine. {NICKNAME}'s important to you, isn't {F#she}{M#he}, Jeht?

732194319.text: #{M#Of course. You're my best friends.}{F#Yeah, I mean, I've always seen you as my... best friend, but I'm just worried that... *sigh* Never mind.}

732194321.text: Yeesh, you're so serious all of a sudden. Paimon doesn't know what to say at all...

732194322.text: Ugh, there's no need to be so awkward! I won't get mad anyhow from now on, and you can count on that!

732194323.text: Hahahaha! That's right, that's the spirit!

732194324.text: Ah, right! About the "Mother of the Jinn"... Is it with you?

732194326.text: Azariq! Didn't Matriarch Babel tell you not to ask that willy-nilly?

732194327.text: It's fine, Jeht! I mean, I guided you half the way, so I count as a "companion," don't I?

732194328.text: A "companion," you say? Perhaps you speak too hastily.

732194330.text: Such insolence! If you recognize me not, then your silence shall serve better!

732194331.text: Whoa, this is a pretty fierce one for sure... Is that the Mother of the Jinn, then?

732194332.text: I'd watch my tongue if I were you, desert-spawn.

732194333.text: This is Azariq, one of my brothers here in the tribe.

732194334.text: Hmph... Well, we could have chosen worse. This one is sturdy enough. A shame that he has too big a mouth, and too small a brain.

732194335.text: *sigh* How is talking to her supposed to *not* end as an exercise in frustration?

732195901.text: #What's the matter, {NICKNAME}? Don't just stand there, let's play some cards. Don't worry! I swear I won't mock you — not even if you're absolutely terrible.

732195902.text: Come on, let's play a round.

732195905.text: Not liking camping out here in the desert, I take it? Haha, oh well... Why don't we tell some stories instead?

732195906.text: You all speak about the interesting things you've heard about, as well as the hair-raising adventures you've been through. Some absolutely ridiculous hearsay is even mixed in...\nThe three of you raise toasts to old triumphs, laugh at ridiculous tales, and shed tears and lament the sad stories.\nAt the end, Azariq closes the proceedings with a joke, and he absolutely kills it.

732195907.text:
#When the moon hangs highest, Azariq tells a rather coarse joke about a crocodile and a Sumpter Beast, which loses him his blanket-sharing privileges.
{M#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
She seems to have lived well amongst the Tanit since your last parting.}{F#Jeht tells you about many trivial but funny things...
A light scent of spices wafts from her, and it seems to you that all the stories she has to tell since your last parting seem tinged with this sadness.}

732195908.text: The night flies by as you chat.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.

732199915.text: Alright! That's one device done and dusted.

732199916.text: Hmm? The door we came through has been sealed. We're going to have to find another way through.

732199922.text: It's said that the destruction of the city was not a deed done from without, but that it fell to revolt from within. That certainly lines up with what we've seen...

732199923.text: Most of the damage was done to the interior. Perhaps it was a slave revolt? Or a civil war between priests?

732199924.text: It could also be the work of long years of disrepair or Wenut activity, right?

732199925.text: Wenut...? I doubt that much at least. Wenut don't dare to touch these ruins, and if the elders are to be believed, that's because this city is "ill-fated."

732199926.text: Alright, enough ghost stories for now. Let's keep going.

732199928.text: Phew, we're back at the temple!

732199929.text: Well, next up, let's get the issue of the large device at the center squared away, shall we?

732199930.text: Ugh... How are you all not dizzy from all this looping around?

732199933.text: Look, there's sand flowing down from the cracks. It seems that some place deeper within the ruins is shaking!

732199942.text: These empty hallways all eventually lead back to the same center. How did the people who worshiped the gods here live...?

732199943.text: Alright, little wildcat. Rather than caring about how now-dead people lived, you should have a care for how you might yet die.

732199944.text: Oh, I have a care for how you might, sure!

732199945.text: Oh? But let me guess — you can't bear to tell me?

732199947.text: You two really do get along nicely...

732199961.text: The blood of outsiders does not mix with that of the tribe, so in many things, I tend to represent something of an "exception"...

732199962.text: And since I've already been to lots of places that are "bad luck," they were fine with sending me to explore this place.

732199963.text: Wait... Aren't they just ostracizing you!?

732199964.text: Well, no... The tribe's just like that. They treat me very well, but I have an outsider's blood. That's all there is to it.

732199965.text: It's just like the book says... "Under the influence of the Jinn, though the land was as a barren desert, it would grow into a verdant oasis..."

732199966.text: Hey, look at that. Isn't there something shiny under that big tree? Could that be the Jinni we're looking for?

732199967.text: Careful, Paimon! We're not sure if this place is safe yet!

732199992.text: Listen. This device has been activated too!

732199993.text: And that's a wrap. Let's go back!
